subject: Performance ledger: onboarding benchmark handoff
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@cardiosense.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom@cardiosense.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding schedule + perf acceptance questions

Hi Neha — thanks again for the runbook template. Before we lock the test window next week, wanted to share the acceptance targets we have internally and confirm Redwood's measurement approach. High level:

• Targets we care about (production-like workload):
  - 95th percentile request latency (inference only): <= 220 ms at steady-state
  - 99th percentile tail latency: <= 500 ms
  - Sustained throughput target: 80 requests/sec (avg request = ~120 tokens)
  - Cold-start recovery within 2s for ephemeral workers

• What we will provide: test corpus (2000 sample requests), API keys for a staging project, and a simple client that simulates our request mix (60% short queries, 30% medium, 10% long).

Can Redwood run the standard ramp, soak, spike set and share: raw telemetry CSV, aggregated percentiles, and the KV cache hit/miss rates? Also please include any example load-shape YAML you intend to run so our infra team can sanity-check.

If these targets look reasonable to Redwood, we can confirm a two-day window (Wed/Thu) and a PO to cover the dedicated test time.

Thanks — Maya
Senior Engineering Manager, CardioSense

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya@cardiosense.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance ledger: onboarding benchmark handoff

Maya — appreciate the clear targets and the corpus plan. We're aligned broadly; couple quick clarifications before we finalize the runbook:

1) Measurement window: Redwood will report inference-only latency (model server → token return) plus end-to-end request latency if you want it. We'll provide both CSV artifacts and a summarized PDF.
2) Warmup: We'll do a 30‑minute warmup (steady 20% of target) before the ramp to populate KV cache and reduce cold-start noise.
3) Test shapes: we'll run three shapes 
   - ramp-to-steady (0 → 80 rps over 10m, hold 45m)
   - soak (80 rps, 2h, steady)
   - spike & recovery (250 rps for 5m, then back to 80)
4) Observability: we'll attach per-request latencies, model-size memory pressure, and KV cache hit/miss by minute.

Action items for CardioSense: please send the staging API key and the test corpus by EOD tomorrow so Monica can stage the load generators.

Cc’ing Monica (CS lead) to schedule the actual run windows and Karthik for tuning notes.

— Neha
Manager, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance ledger: onboarding benchmark handoff

Adding technical detail for the runbook so the load engineers can prepare. Key notes:

- Batch sizing: we will start with dynamic batching (max batch = 32) and instrument average batch size; if you prefer fixed batch sizes for determinism we can lock to 16.
- KV cache config: TTL 10m for request prefixes, pre-populate top 200 recent keys from your corpus during warmup.
- Quantization: CardioSense model variant? If you're using a 4-bit quantized variant, we'll run both fp16 and 4-bit runs; expected throughput delta ~1.7x. Please confirm model artifact name.
- Concurrency: target 10 worker threads per GPU for steady 80 rps; spike runs will open additional ephemeral workers.

Proposed load-shape snippet (we'll push full YAML to the Drive link once you confirm):

  - name: ramp-to-steady
    start_rps: 0
    end_rps: 80
    duration: 600

  - name: soak
    rps: 80
    duration: 7200

  - name: spike
    rps: 250
    duration: 300

If we see 99th-percentile spikes during soak, step 1 is to verify KV cache hit-rate and then raise warmup to 60 minutes if necessary.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya@cardiosense.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance ledger: onboarding benchmark handoff

Maya — we ran the three shapes as discussed this morning in staging. Summary below; full artifacts attached.

Quick summary (attachments: cardiosense-load-report-20261112.csv, kv-cache-telemetry-20261112.json):
• Ramp-to-steady: reached 80 rps in 9m30s, steady-state med latency = 86 ms, 95p = 210 ms, 99p = 480 ms. KV cache hit-rate at steady: 78%.
• Soak (2h): average throughput 79.2 rps; 95p = 215 ms (within target), 99p = 540 ms (exceeded target by 40 ms). We observed tail spikes correlated with periodic GC/eviction cycles on worker 3.
• Spike: system handled 250 rps for 5m; recovery to 80 rps median latency within 6s (slightly over cold-start requirement).

Notes and remediation plan:
1) Tail latency: root cause appears to be periodic cache eviction + a GC pause on a single worker. Proposed fix: extend warmup to 60m in production simulation, and adjust KV TTL to 15m for this workload.
2) Cold-starts: reduce ephemeral worker spin-up time by pre-warming small pool during spike windows.
3) Next steps: if CardioSense can accept conditional signoff (95p okay; 99p requires mitigation tracked in the action log), we'll schedule a second verification run after config tweak.

Please review the CSV and KV telemetry attached. If you accept conditional signoff we will produce an acceptance packet (short PDF + artifacts) and move to final onboarding tasks (billing + production cutover checklist).

— Monica
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cardiosense-load-report-20261112.csv (7.8MB), kv-cache-telemetry-20261112.json (420KB)

From: Maya Rao <maya@cardiosense.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom@cardiosense.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance ledger: onboarding benchmark handoff

Thanks team — appreciate the quick run and clear notes. CardioSense is comfortable with a conditional signoff. Two asks before we greenlight the acceptance packet:

1) Please run the shortened verification after the TTL/warmup change (we're fine with a 2-hour soak).
2) Share the acceptance packet draft (one-page summary + the artifacts) and an itemized list for the post-cutover checklist (billing cadence, rollback playbook, SLA contacts).

We'll queue the PO for the two-day test block pending the verification run results. If the verification shows the 99p within 500ms, we will sign the onboarding acceptance and request production cutover date.

— Maya
Senior Engineering Manager, CardioSense
